items.response:
Here's the lemon loaf in grams, using standard conversions, so treat them as close rather than exact:
- Flour 1 1/2 cups: about 190 g
- Sugar 1 cup: about 200 g
- Butter 1/2 cup: about 113 g
- Plain yogurt 1/2 cup: about 125 g
- Lemon juice 2 tbsp: about 30 g
- Baking powder 1 tsp: about 4 g
Action: I'll save this conversion to your notes next to the recipe so it's there when you bake.

On it. I'll put together a 15-item spring cleaning checklist and save it in Notes. For the couch, I'll look for junk removal or bulk pickup options and prices, and since it's in the basement I'll ask about stairs and the removal crew's fee for that.
Action: Draft the checklist into Notes, then pull 2-3 couch haul-away options with prices and earliest dates for you to pick from before I book anything.

Sure. You promised Tom the Instant Payouts launch readiness review doc by 28 Oct, a week before GA, so it's worth knowing what's still open on it. I'll go through the open comments, the linked tickets and anything carried over from the last review, and list what's unresolved.
Action: Open the readiness doc in Notion and send you a short list of unresolved comments, open linked tickets and leftover review items, with the 28 Oct deadline in mind.

Sorry for Hannah, that's a miserable surprise. In general she'll need to find out which impound lot has the car (by calling the city's towing/parking enforcement line or the tow company named on any notice), then go in person with photo ID, proof of ownership and insurance, and pay the tow and storage fees. Storage charges build up daily, so she should go soon. I don't want to quote fees from memory, so I'll check the current ones.
Action: Look up the current Toronto tow and impound process and fees for a street-cleaning tow, and check whether she can contest the tow if the signage was unclear, then send you a short summary for her.

Will do. Going by your Vancouver dates of 9 to 13 July, I'll text Hannah something like: 'Hi Hannah, you kindly offered to help with Biscuit. Could you feed and walk him while we're away 9-13 July? We'll pay you, of course. He eats Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach (salmon), so no chicken-based food or treats please, since it makes his skin itchy. No worries at all if it doesn't work.'
Action: Send that text to Hannah now and tell you as soon as she replies.

Lovely idea. Since you met at a friend's board-game night in 2015, a cozy at-home board game night after Leo's asleep fits well: pull out a game you'd both enjoy, make a couple of snacks and drinks, and maybe swap short notes about your first impressions. I'd skip the candles and use soft lamps or string lights, so nothing strongly scented sets off Sam's migraines. I have two different anniversary dates saved, so I won't build anything around that date.
Action: Turn this into a simple plan with a short shopping list, and ask you which game and snacks you'd like.

Got it, I'll keep replies short today.
Action: Short answers from now on, with details only if you ask.

Great idea for a do-over, and a board-game theme suits how you two met. Since it has to be a Saturday, I'll look for a board-game cafe or a game night out with good vegetarian options, as Sam is vegetarian and doesn't eat fish or seafood. I'll also need to know which Saturdays work for you, and whether you want childcare arranged for Leo.
Action: Find 2-3 board-game dinner options with vegetarian menus and Saturday availability, check your calendar for open Saturdays, and bring you a shortlist before I book anything.

Happy early birthday to Leo! I don't know what Wonder Workshop's party sizes or prices are, so I'll check their current packages for Saturday 23 Jan 2027, for twelve kids.
Action: Look up Wonder Workshop on Queen East for party capacity, packages, cost, deposit and availability on 23 Jan 2027, and send you the details.

I don't have that search saved, so I can't tell you what we found, and I don't want to guess times or fares. I can redo the Friday-evening Toronto to Ottawa search now, though the times and prices may differ from back then.
Action: Pull current VIA Rail Friday evening departures and fares from Toronto to Ottawa and compare them with driving time, then send you the comparison.

Happy to find one. For the subjunctive at upper-intermediate (B2) level, I'll look for a grammar book with plenty of exercises and a full answer key, and compare a few options. I'd like to show you the shortlist with prices before I order.
Action: Search for 2-3 upper-intermediate Spanish grammar books focused on the subjunctive with answer keys, and bring you the options with price and delivery time.

Sorry about the heel, that sounds like it needs a look, especially after a long run. I'll find a physio for next week, after work or on Saturday, but I don't have a regular physio saved for you, so I'll check nearby clinics with availability for heel pain.
Action: Search nearby physio clinics with weekday evening or Saturday openings next week, check them against your calendar, and send you 2-3 options before booking.

Sorry about Sam's migraine, and that's a tricky spot to be in. Since Grace teaches piano and Daniel is a retired civil engineer, here are unscented ideas: a nice book or sheet music collection for Grace, and a book on bridges or local engineering history for Daniel, plus something to share like local maple syrup or honey, or good chocolates, and no soaps, candles or anything perfumed. I still need to check what's open near Alta Vista tomorrow.
Action: Look up what's open tomorrow near Alta Vista for a bookstore or gift shop, and send you 2-3 unscented options for them.

Close, but not close enough to rely on. Written Portuguese is fairly readable if you know Spanish, but spoken Portuguese, especially the European kind you'll hear in Lisbon, sounds quite different, so your Spanish will help you less than you'd expect for listening and speaking. Plenty of people there speak some English too.
Action: Add a short list of survival Portuguese phrases and pronunciation tips to your Lisbon plan, and keep the days to one main activity plus a quiet afternoon break as you asked.

Morning! I can't tell yet. I see Home Depot order #W512339870 for the 16x25x1 furnace filters (pack of 4), set for pickup at the Leslie St store, but nothing here shows whether you collected them.
Action: Check the order status and your email for a pickup confirmation, and tell you whether they were picked up. If not, I'll remind you to collect them.

Happy to, and congrats on the beta wrapping up. For eight of us, Wen is vegan, so I'll need a place with solid vegan options and good vegetarian ones too. Saffron Lane on Queen Street East is your favourite for South Indian food, so I'll check whether it's close enough to the office and takes a group of eight, but I'll also look for other options. Since this is a lunch, I'll need the time you want.
Action: Shortlist 3 places near the office with vegan options and room for 8 next Thursday, and check with you on the lunch time before booking.

Sending the text to Rui now. For Saturday the 14th, Valentine's Day is a busy night, so I'll look for a table for four in Leslieville or Riverside within walking distance of your place. I'll need a time and any food restrictions for the other couple, so I'll check availability first.
Action: Send the draft to Rui, then find 3 restaurants in Leslieville or Riverside with a table for four on Sat 14 Feb and send you the options before booking.

Here's a draft for the week back, with the big one first: Nate's cabinet delivery is Thu 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00, and someone needs to be home. Thursday is normally an office day on King Street West, so you'd work from home or have Sam cover. Also: change the furnace filter (16x25x1, due every three months), and since it'll get properly cold soon, check windows and doors for drafts and put the outdoor hoses away. The upstairs bathroom door sticks in humid weather, so that's low priority.
Action: Save this list in your notes and block Thu 16 Oct 8:00-10:00 as 'home for cabinet delivery' on your calendar.

I can't tell you from what's in front of me, and I don't want to guess times or counts. I'd need to check the calendar records for Tom's February availability and the log of the May school-calendar sync.
Action: Look up Tom's free slots on the day in question in February (tell me the date if you have it) and find how many of Sam's school events were imported in the May sync, then report back.

October 2025 groceries came to $972.55 across 16 transactions, the lowest of the three months. August was $1,108.42 (about $136 more) and September was $1,346.29 (about $374 more, including a $312.44 Costco run on Sep 27). The three-month average is $1,142.42.
Action: I can break October down by store if you want it.

Sure. Here's the general checklist for renewing a child's passport: Leo's current passport, a completed child application form, two passport photos, a guarantor's details, and proof of citizenship or parental ID if required. The parent or guardian signs and pays the fee. Since it expires in January, we should apply soon to leave time for processing. I'll confirm the current rules and fees before you rely on this.
Action: Check the official requirements and fees, then look up the nearest passport office or Service Canada appointment availability and send you a checklist with appointment options.

I can draft the text, but I don't have the fire truck story saved, so I can't say what happened last time. Can you remind me? I'd write Hannah something like: 'Thanks so much for taking Biscuit tomorrow morning. We'll drop him at [time] with his food and leash, he needs [walk/feeding details], and if sirens go by he may panic, so please hold the leash tight.' I'll fill in the real details after you confirm what they are.
Action: Hold the draft until you tell me the drop-off time, feeding and walk details, and what happened with the sirens, then send it to Hannah.

Here's the list for the week you're back: Thursday 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00, Nate's cabinet delivery, so someone needs to be home to let the crew in. Then winter prep before it gets properly cold: check the furnace filter, look for window and door drafts, and put away outdoor hoses and garden things. I can add anything specific you have in mind.
Action: Save this list in your notes and block Thu 16 Oct 8:00-10:00 on your calendar for the delivery.

Sure. I'll build a simple cart with PC Express's no-name staples: fruit, crackers, cheese or yogurt, popcorn and veggie sticks with dip, all nut-free because of Leo's tree nut allergy. Before I check out, can you tell me if Jun or his sister have any allergies?
Action: Build the cart for three kids, set pickup for tomorrow at 3:00 pm, and place the order once you confirm no other allergies.

Dinosaur it is! I'll look for a size 7 dinosaur costume under $50 that will be delivered before Friday 30 Jan, so I'm checking delivery times as well as price.
Action: Search for size 7 dinosaur costumes under $50 with delivery by Thu 29 Jan, and order the best-rated one that fits those limits, then send you the details.

I can't see that link in what I have, so I can't give you the price yet. Once I have it I'll check the cost and compare it with typical prices for a similar saree, though silk and zari work vary a lot, so I'll give you a range rather than a verdict.
Action: Look for the saved Kanchi Silks link in your notes and bookmarks, and if I can't find it, ask you to send it. Then check the price and compare it with similar sarees.

Sweet of you. I'll order an oat-milk flat white for Sam, with no hazelnut, and a vegetarian snack with no fish or seafood. Schools often have a front-office drop-off rule, so I'll check whether they can take it to room 214 or should leave it at the office.
Action: Find a cafe that delivers to Riverdale around 3:30 and order the coffee and a vegetarian snack, with a note for room 214, then confirm the details with you.

Happy long weekend! Here's your checklist for today:
- [ ] Fix Leo's bike chain
- [ ] Hang the hallway mirror
- [ ] Sort the garage recycling
- [ ] Plant the tomato seedlings
- [ ] Find the good extension cord
Action: Save it to your notes as today's checklist.

I'll reorder the dishwasher pods and paper towels, matching what you bought last time. For the Dyson, I'd like to know which model Hannah has, since there are a few cordless ones at different prices, and I don't want to buy something that expensive without asking you.
Action: Reorder the pods and paper towels, then send you 2-3 cordless Dyson options with prices, so you can pick before I buy anything.

Tom had two free slots on 24 Feb 2026: 10:00-10:30 and 15:30-16:00. For the May sync, 14 events were imported from Sam's school calendar on 28 May 2026.
Action: None needed unless you want me to use those for the pricing review write-up.

Looking at your records, you already ordered 'Gramática de uso del español B1-B2' from Indigo (delivered 3 Oct 2025), so before I buy another book I'd like to know whether you want something beyond that. For the subjunctive at upper-intermediate level, I'll check Indigo and other Canadian retailers first rather than Amazon, and look for a book with exercises and an answer key. Since you learn best through role-play and want Mexican rather than Castilian vocabulary, I can add role-play drills to go with the book.
Action: Shortlist 2-3 B2 subjunctive books from Canadian retailers with answer keys and prices, and check with you before ordering.

I don't have your account data in front of me, so I won't guess. I'd need to check your statements for recurring and automatic payments apart from bills, and look at the Amazon order status for the batteries. For history, all I can see is this recent session: the data request draft for Wen, your week summary and your Vancouver flight preferences. I can't show a complete history from here.
Action: Pull the recurring charges from your TD and Visa statements, check the Amazon batteries order tracking, and see what history I can retrieve, then report back.

Lovely idea. I don't have how you two met saved, so tell me the story and I'll build a plan around it. Meanwhile, some at-home ideas once Leo's asleep: recreate the setting with the food, drinks or music from back then, write each other a short letter about your first impressions and swap them over dessert, or cook the first meal you ever made together.
Action: Wait for the story of how you met, then turn the best idea into a plan with a shopping list.

Sunday scaries are the worst, and the extra hour didn't help. Tomorrow is manageable. The only open item is picking a slot for the 30-minute payout edge-case chat with Aisha and Diego, and I can take care of that.
Action: Hold off on anything else tonight, and tell me which slot you want (or say 'pick one') and I'll send the invite.

Sure. I don't want to give Olivia a GA date or a merchant list that isn't confirmed, especially before a prospect call, so I'll check what's actually decided on the Instant Payouts rollout beyond the beta merchants. I'll draft the reply for you to review.
Action: Search Notion, Linear and Slack for the current GA timing and beta expansion plan, then draft a reply to Olivia and show it to you before sending.

A simple structure works best: one shared database that anyone on the team can add to, with a weekly triage view. Starting fields: Date, Source (support email, sales call, reply to updates), Merchant, Feedback summary, Category (bug, UX, missing feature, pricing, other), Severity, Linked ticket, Owner, Status (new, triaged, planned, done), and Triage notes. Add a weekly 'to triage' view and a short guide for where each source gets logged.
Action: Create this as a database in Notion (or Linear if your team prefers) with the 'to triage' view, leave it unshared until you've reviewed it, and send you the link.

I can't judge it until I've read the email, so I'll go through it first. Going by your goals, you're at B1 working toward B2, with the DELE B2 in May 2026 and a plan to hold an hour-long conversation without English before Mexico City in 2027. More speaking time with Carlos would help with that. Your current lessons are $180 for four, which is $45 each, so I'll compare cost per lesson, your Thursday 8:00 pm lesson, and the schedule.
Action: Read Carlos's email, then send you a short verdict on whether it's worth it, with cost and calendar conflicts.

I don't have the episode in front of me, so I can't name it from memory. I'll look through my earlier summaries and notes for a developer-platform pricing episode.
Action: Search your notes and past summaries for it and send you the title and link to forward to Aisha. If I can't find it, I'll ask you for the show name.

I don't have Biscuit's birth date or behavioural notes saved, and I don't want to put guesses on a vet form. His adoption paperwork or old vaccine records likely show the date, and for the notes, the vet usually wants things like triggers, how he reacts to strangers and handling, and any anxiety.
Action: Search your files and emails for his adoption papers or vaccine records to find the birth date, and ask you for the behavioural details so I can draft the notes for you to check.

That sounds really draining. You finally had a nice day with Leo, and one message on a Saturday evening pulled your brain back into Looker. It makes sense that you hate how easily that happens.
Action: Just listen for now. Tell me more if you want, and I'll hold off on suggestions unless you ask.

Here's a quick version for Priya. Pros: better retention and hiring appeal, rested and more focused staff, and often similar output in fewer hours. Cons: client deadlines and meetings squeezed into four days, a risk of longer days, coverage gaps, and questions about pay and billable hours in a firm like hers. A trial period with clear measures would be a good middle step.
Action: Put that into a short message to Priya for you to edit, and send it only once you approve.

Here's a simple answer for Leo: poppies grew on the battlefields of World War I in Flanders, where the ground had been churned up. A Canadian doctor, Lt.-Col. John McCrae, wrote the poem 'In Flanders Fields' in 1915 after losing a friend, and it made the poppy a symbol of remembering the soldiers who died. We wear one on Remembrance Day, 11 November, to say we remember them.
Action: I can write a shorter, kid-friendly version for Leo if you want one.

I'll reorder the dishwasher pods and paper towels, since household staples can go through, and I'll look at Canadian retailers first rather than Amazon where something ships within a week. The Dyson is a bigger purchase and likely over $150, so I'll find options and ask you before buying. Do you know which model Hannah has?
Action: Reorder the pods and paper towels, then send you 2-3 cordless Dyson options with prices from Canadian retailers, and wait for your go-ahead.

Added, owner you: update the public roadmap page for the multi-currency wallets postponement to H1 2027. On Prince Edward County, Sandbanks, two wineries, the cheese shop, Lake on the Mountain and the lavender farm all on Saturday after leaving at 8 is a very full day with the drive each way, so I'd move one stop to Sunday. Sam driving means a long day behind the wheel too, and tastings may be limited.
Action: Add the roadmap action item with you as owner, then check opening hours and booking needs for each stop and send you a Saturday timeline showing whether it fits.

That sounds exhausting. A message like that on a Saturday evening can hijack the whole day, and it's frustrating when you were finally having a good one with Leo. I'm here to listen, and if you want, I can also draft a short holding reply for Tom so you can let it go until Monday.
Action: Wait for you. Tell me if you want to keep venting or want me to draft the reply.
